key_insight: Policy-coupled coverage links uncertainty sets directly to the action they induce, making counterfactual decision-making both statistically valid and utility-optimal.
engineering_relevance: For high-stakes ML systems in treatment, policy, or marketing settings, this provides a principled way to choose actions while preserving finite-sample coverage guarantees.
method: Define prediction sets whose coverage is measured on the realized outcome under the chosen action.
Use a max-min / risk-averse decision rule that is minimax-optimal under distributional ambiguity.
Implement a two-stage conformal procedure (PC-RACP) to approximate the optimal sets with rigorous finite-sample coverage.
evidence_signal: The paper reports simulations and a real email-marketing experiment showing PC-RACP improves utility over existing methods while maintaining valid coverage.
watch_item: The approach depends on correctly modeling the counterfactual decision structure; mis-specified utilities or action spaces can reduce the practical value of the guarantees.
paper_title: Prediction Sets for Counterfactual Decisions: Coverage, Optimality, and Conformal Prediction
